questions.stem:
Consider the following code segment.

```text
x ← 3
total ← 0
REPEAT 6 TIMES
{
   x ← x + 1
   IF (x MOD 2 = 0)
   {
      total ← total + x
   }
}
DISPLAY (total)
```

What is displayed as a result of running the code segment?

options.why: Correct. x goes from 4 to 9; the multiples of 2 among them are added.
Recheck which values are multiples of 2.
total adds the values, not 1 each time.
Only values divisible by 2 are added.

questions.explanation: The values of x are 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9; the multiples of 2 add to 18.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all possible values of `RANDOM(1, 7) * 2 + 7`?

options.why: Correct. RANDOM gives 1 to 7; doubling and adding 7 gives every second number from 9 to 21.
The result is doubled before adding.
Doubling skips every other number.
RANDOM(1, n) starts at 1, not 0.

questions.stem: A sorted list contains 100,003 elements. What is the maximum number of elements that binary search must examine to find a value or determine it is not in the list?

options.why: Correct. Each check halves the remaining elements; about 17 checks reduce 100,003 to none.
2 to the power 17 is already more than 100003.
Binary search halves the remaining range at every step.
That is the worst case for linear search.

questions.explanation: 2^16 = 65536 is less than 100003 but 2^17 = 131072 is not, so at most 17 checks are needed.

questions.stem: A network has computers P, Q, R, S, T, U. The direct connections are: P–R, P–U, Q–U, R–T, R–U, S–T, S–U. What is the minimum number of connections that must fail for computer S to be unable to communicate with computer U?

options.why: After that many failures a path still remains.
Correct. Removing 2 well-chosen connections separates S from U; removing fewer always leaves a path.
Some set of 2 connections already disconnects them.
Look for the fewest connections whose failure leaves no path.

questions.explanation: S has 2 connections and U has 4. Checking failures systematically shows that 2 is the fewest that leaves no path between them.
